messages:
Priya (PM): Quick sync — we got 3 field asks this week asking for a deterministic upgrade path for on-prem + clearer VPC handoff docs. Can we map Q2 priorities?
Sam (Eng): TL;DR: customers want zero-downtime upgrades, clear compatibility matrix, and a small installer footprint.
Maya (Eng-Infra): Agree. The big risk is KV cache migration between versions. Need a proposal: in-place migration vs side-by-side rollouts.
Jordan (Solutions): From field: customers are fine with a brief connection drain window if we provide a rollback plan + automation. They want scripted handoff for customer-managed NAT/firewall rules.
Erin (Network): We can provide recommended firewall rules and an iptable snippet, but some corp networks insist on inbound-only egress. Need guidance on port whitelists + healthcheck endpoints.
Priya (PM): Can we list deliverables for Q2? My draft: 1) Upgrade playbook (in-place + side-by-side), 2) VPC handoff checklist + sample iptables, 3) Minimal airgap installer for constrained customers, 4) Compatibility matrix for model/runtime variants.
Sam (Eng): Sounds right. For playbook, propose we support: - minor upgrades in-place w/ DB schema migrations scripted - major upgrades via canary side-by-side + traffic switch.
Maya (Eng-Infra): Implementation notes: we should include a persistent KV migration tool that can do streaming migration (delta-first) and a safe-check mode. We can reuse parts of the migration library from Dedicated.
Jordan (Solutions): Add a customer-facing runbook snippet: ```
# Drain, migrate, verify
redwoodctl drain --service private-deploy
redwoodctl migrate-kv --from v1.9 --to v2.0 --verify
redwoodctl resume --service private-deploy
```
Erin (Network): Also add network verification steps: curl health endpoints from bastion, confirm TLS handshake to KMS, and validate egress rules for telemetry.
Priya (PM): Launch criteria idea: 1) Migration tool validated on 3 internal clusters, 2) Runbook tested with two pilot customers, 3) Automated rollback completes in <15m, 4) Docs and iptable snippets reviewed by security. Thoughts?
Sam (Eng): Rollback <15m is doable for minor versions. Major rollback timelines depend on model weights and disk transfer times — need an MLP (max roll back plan) that includes estimated time per GB.
Maya (Eng-Infra): We should include a 'fast-fail' mode where new nodes are quarantined and traffic stays on stable nodes until KV sync completes. That reduces blast radius.
Jordan (Solutions): Field ask: a one-click checklist for sysadmins. Even if internal, deliver a CLI that runs preflight checks and prints a friendly "all good" or a list of failures.
Priya (PM): OK — prioritize preflight CLI + runbook + network checklist for the first sprint. Airgap installer can follow but we need a spec now.
Erin (Network): For VPC handoff, propose sections: required routes, endpoints, healthcheck paths, TLS cert management, and flow logs. Provide example terraform snippet for VPC peering.
Sam (Eng): Terraform snippet example is quick. But keep in mind customers use different providers — AWS, GCP, Azure. We'll provide provider-specific extras in docs.
Maya (Eng-Infra): Dependencies: we need a small test harness to run upgrade+rollback in CI and a couple of infra fixtures that simulate restricted networks. I can spin up a harness in the next sprint.
DevOpsBot: Deployment pipeline note: created pipeline run #452 for upgrade-playbook tests, logs at https://ci.redwood/infrastructure/452 :white_check_mark:
Jordan (Solutions): Can we set success criteria for pilot customers? e.g., pilot A (enterprise) will test in-place minor upgrade; pilot B (startup) will run side-by-side major upgrade. Need volunteers for outreach.
Priya (PM): I'll own pilot coordination. Sam/Maya, can you commit to the migration tool v0.1 and preflight CLI by end of sprint 2?
Sam (Eng): Yes, will aim for v0.1 — API for migrate-kv + simulate mode.
Maya (Eng-Infra): I'll build the test harness and the fast-fail node quarantine feature.
Erin (Network): I'll draft the VPC handoff checklist and example iptables/terraform snippets.
Priya (PM): Great. Last thing: scope negotiation — advisors say keep airgap installer out of initial GA unless a large customer signs up. We'll document the spec but move it to backlog if no signoff. Agree?
Jordan (Solutions): Agree — keep GA focused and deliverable.
Priya (PM): Cool. I'll update the roadmap doc, create tickets for: MIGRATE-123 (migration tool), PREFLT-45 (preflight CLI), HANDF-67 (VPC handoff + docs), TESTH-99 (test harness). I'll ping owners. :thumbsup:
Sam (Eng): Thanks. Quick question — do we include quantization/weights compatibility in the matrix?
Maya (Eng-Infra): Yes — add columns: model format, quantization profile, runtime ABI. That prevents surprises during upgrades.
Priya (PM): Perfect. Meeting adjourned. I'll post the roadmap update and link tickets here.
Jordan (Solutions): Thanks all.
Erin (Network): Thanks!
